neighbours.label: A term handled as a defined or graded item inside a formal standard, classification or indicator system (control 'defined as' in an accounting standard, a 'Group 1' category, a governance indicator); quiet on the same words in everyday use
fire: Under the reporting standard, control over an investee is defined as the power to direct its activities.
The cancer agency lists diesel exhaust as a Group 1 agent, the highest level of evidence.
In the national accounts, control over a corporation is defined as the ability to set its general policy.
The transparency index showed that corruption was still a grave problem in the public sector.
Under the labelling system, the substance falls in Category 1 for acute toxicity.
For tax purposes, effective control over a subsidiary is defined as holding more than half of the votes.
The panel placed the solvent in Group 2 of its classification, meaning a probable cause of cancer.
According to the governance indicators, corruption was a severe obstacle to doing business.
quiet: On the wet road, the driver lost control of the van and hit a fence.
The tour guide split the visitors into a small group for the cave walk.
She kept careful control of the budget all year.
The film is about corruption in a small police station.
The children fell into the river and were pulled out by a farmer.
For most people, a quiet evening means a book and a cup of tea.
The coach placed the new player in the second row for the photo.
According to the neighbours, the party was a great success.
